instructions: Writ trail, first link. Where Devan checks the oilcloth before sleep, keep the writ in his pack. Change the comparison 'rather than leave it in the shutter frame' to 'rather than leave it in the hollow behind the third slat at Kettamala'. From now on the hiding place has one name everywhere: the hollow behind the third slat (of the warden's chamber shutter). Chapters 21 and 30 follow this trail.
Number drift. Wherever the text says Devan made the drill at twenty-five and is thirty-two, keep 'seven years' as the canonical span. Make sure no other number appears for it in this chapter.
Keep the drill as written: a slow, one-handed, two-finger strike stopped a hair short of the post. Chapter 32 now builds its left-hand drill from this strike, so don't change it.
Keep 'He cuts himself, I get the welt... That's all of it. It's also everything.' and Devan's interior reaction exactly as they are. The owner singled this beat out.

Sanu must be unambiguously adult at his first appearance. Cut the 'young Sanu' phrasing in the drying-shed introduction. Give his age on the page, as a plain fact in Neela's POV or in dialogue (for example 'Sanu, twenty-six, Fourth Guard, who still blushed when Usha said his name'). Choose twenty-six so it matches the chapter 16 date fix: sold at seven, intake nineteen years back.
Scan the other guard introductions (Sajan, Lata) and remove any wording that reads as adolescent. Each of them is a serving adult guard.

Sanu's intake date. Change 'Sold at seven... The date, six years back' to 'nineteen years back', so a seven-year-old intake makes him twenty-six now, matching chapter 12. If the page reading lingers on his childhood, keep it to the sale fact. Add nothing that frames him as young in the present.

Repetition. 'Did not look away' and 'her eyes did not change' recur heavily. Keep at most one of each in the chapter. Replace the rest with concrete action that shows the same steadiness: the queen squaring the writing case to the table edge, Usha's hand flat on her folded page, Neela not lowering the page she holds.

If the line 'She was fifty-four. Neela knew the number as she knew the sum of a lock's pins' appears here, cut it. Neela has no way to know the age. If the age matters, have someone who would know say it (Usha), or cut the number entirely.

Protect the midpoint. Keep the fresh page in tacky ink with the fly stuck in it. Keep 'You carried away paper. You can't carry away what I saw.' Keep the click of Chathu's rat-eaten page and Kamalakshi's question, the plain-ink clue that slides away, and 'The only freedom I have ever had is the one that bleeds when he does.' Don't trim these while fixing repetition.
Kamalakshi's quips. If she has a one-word quip in this chapter, check it against chapters 30 to 32 under the same rule: one quip per stretch of adjacent chapters, and any extra becomes a gesture.

Consistency with the Sanu age fix. Where Sanu says he wants to name himself to his brother, make nothing in the line imply a boy. If he or the narration mentions how long he has served, it must fit nineteen years since intake. Cut any 'young Sanu' or 'the boy' phrasing.

Writ trail, second link. At dawn Neela opens the hollow behind the third slat (use that name, not 'the hollow in the shutter frame'). The chit and the gift seal are still inside. The writ is not there, because Devan has carried it in his pack since chapter 2. He takes the oilcloth from his pack and lays the writ in the hollow beside the chit and seal while she watches, where it lived before. Then he says he will read it aloud before the queen. Keep the slat's creak from Muthu's line ('The slat still creaks. I didn't fix it either').

Plant Asha's scrap here, openly. In the hollow, under the camphor block that keeps the insects off the papers, Devan finds a scrap in Asha's hand: 'Say it anyway.' He knows the hand because she wrote his letters (chapter 11). He reads it aloud to Neela at once and tells her where he found it. Make it a small, quiet beat, a few lines. Its job is to give chapter 30 a planted motive and to keep their no-secrets term intact: he hides nothing from her.
Keep the rest of the chapter's bargain as outlined: lamp lit, being seen as a choice, the refusal split between them.

Sanu's self-naming to Kandan. By now Sanu's adulthood is stated in chapter 12. Add nothing here that frames him as young. If the rite description touches him physically or emotionally, keep the framing as comrades and adults. Cut any 'boy' or 'young' wording in the naming dusk.

Number drift. Change 'let no one at his back for six years' so it agrees with the seven-year drill span from chapter 2. Use 'seven years'. If the series bible dates Asha's death to a different year than the drill, drop the number and write 'since Asha', so no second count appears to drift.
Keep the queen's single word 'Yes.' as her first admission. It is the first of the three confession beats, and it stays short. Don't expand it, so chapters 30 and 31 each carry a distinct, new act.
Writ trail, final link. Keep Devan lifting the writ from 'the hollow behind the third slat'. This now matches chapters 2 and 21.

Asha's scrap. Cut 'a scrap he found under a camphor block... kept it from Neela for weeks' and any other line saying he withheld it. The scrap was found in chapter 21 and read aloud to Neela then. Where the chapter calls back to it, refer to it as shared ('the scrap she had heard him read at dawn in the warden's chamber'). Let 'Say it anyway' drive his choice to read the writ and to declare himself, as a motive they both know.
Cut the aside 'I know the hand from a letter shown at a border school.' Let the evidence climax run without it.

Trim the queen's public confession. She has already said 'Yes' in chapter 29, and chapter 31's charter reading is where the list of crimes is read aloud. Cut the ledger-style list (raids permitted, the thirty bought, his death paid for) from this speech. Keep only the new material: 'It is only blind' and 'I only found out this week I could do it standing,' with Usha's welts on her arm as the visible proof. A few lines at most.

In the same speech, change 'twenty-six of my own knives knelt... bleeding for strangers' so they bleed for people they chose, for example '...knelt in the dark and chose who they would bleed for.' Choice is the point.

Protect: the self-naming with backs turned, 'A witness's knowledge with the witnessing taken out', Janu and Kamalakshi ('You've a face like a wall already'), and Devan's declaration ('never in front of her like a wall'). Keep all three as they are.

Kamalakshi's quips. Chapters 30, 31 and 32 carry her one-word quips ('About time', 'Finally') close together. Keep the first one that occurs across these chapters. Turn every later one into a gesture specific to her: a slap of the table, an elbow in Janu's ribs, a slow clap no one else joins. If this chapter holds the second quip, it becomes the gesture.
If the 'She was fifty-four... sum of a lock's pins' line appears here, cut it or source the age through a character who would know.

Charter reading. The queen's confession moves here as the act itself. When she reads the clause naming what the crown permitted, make this the first time the full list is spoken in public: the controlled raids, the stolen children of Nellimala, the payment for Devan's death, Asha's killing. Give it its weight: the hall's silence, Rema's pen, the queen reading in daylight and not stopping. It now carries charge because chapter 30 no longer spends it.

Dawn count. Replace 'Seven breaths from the first of the grey. Yours catches at the ninth count' with one plain line from Devan: 'You hitch at nine. I've counted it every morning since the wedding.' Let Neela's surprise (that he counted every morning, not that he counts) carry the beat in a line or two of reaction, then move on.

Ending. Cut the stranger climbing at grey entirely. End the chapter on 'Then she helped him find his sleeve.' (she dressing him at dawn after the hitch count), with no hook line after it. Chapter 32 no longer opens on the deflation.
Protect 'Neela. May I put my hand here.' and the bargain change around his dead hand exactly as written.
Apply the Kamalakshi quip rule from chapter 30: one quip across chapters 30 to 32, the rest gestures. If this chapter holds a quip that is not the first, make it a gesture.
If the 'She was fifty-four...' line appears here, cut it or source it.

Opening. Remove the line that deflates chapter 31's stranger ('turned out to be a boy... with wet sandals') and any reference to that stranger. Open straight on weeks on: the truce sailing and the hall with its lamp.

Drill. Replace 'a slow open-handed pattern... that needed both hands' with a new left-hand drill built from the old one-handed two-finger strike, for example 'a left-handed drill he had built out of the old two-finger strike, the two fingers opened into a parry and slowed until the young could follow.' Keep the seventh-day round with Muthu, Devan losing, and laughing first.

Number drift. Change every 'eight years' ('eight years of a drill', 'one in eight years') to seven, matching chapter 2. The 'eight years deciding everything alone' line is replaced entirely under the final-scene fix below.

Final scene at the door. Cut the passage where Neela thinks 'You do not put the question that matters to a stranger at your door...' and then gives the envoy a full speech. That breaks the vote culture and reads as pulling rank. Keep 'How do you vote?' / 'You first.' exactly. Then she answers Devan alone, low, out of the envoy's hearing: her lean (no) and her reason (Nellimala, the camp in her village's footings). Then she turns to the envoy and says only: 'We'll hear you at the table. Leave your staff at the door. We vote at noon.'

Replace the narrated line 'the face of a man who had spent eight years deciding everything alone, and had chosen... to wait for her' with something he does. For example: after 'You first' he steps back half a pace so she stands alone in the lamplight of the doorway, and he lifts his good hand off the doorpost and keeps it lowered while she speaks.

River echo (C13). Add one line, without resolving it, so the series thread isn't dropped. For example, Koman the watcher mentions at the door that the long, low shape was in the river below the pass again at dawn, taking nothing, watching the road. Place it before the envoy arrives so it doesn't compete with the hinge.
Apply the Kamalakshi quip rule: one quip across chapters 30 to 32, the rest gestures.
If the 'She was fifty-four...' line appears here, cut it or source it.

notes_not_actioned.note: Ch 31 end: end on 'Then she helped him find his sleeve.' with Kuttu's horn calling the first vote
notes_not_actioned.why: Chapter 32 opens weeks later and holds the Company's first vote, so a horn calling it at chapter 31's dawn would break the timeline. The stranger is cut and the chapter ends cleanly on the sleeve line, which takes the note's alternative option.
